edits.text: Engineered Demo Commerce, a self-directed eight-week prototype (2025; not launched), implementing buyer onboarding, rules-based (non-ML) lead scoring, and pricing controls and integrating payment setup.

Built GTM workflow automation in Demo Commerce, a self-directed eight-week prototype (2025; not launched), implementing rules-based lead scoring to support lead qualification alongside buyer onboarding and pricing controls.
Implemented buyer-facing onboarding and commerce setup in Demo Commerce, a self-directed eight-week prototype (2025; not launched), including pricing controls and a payment setup integration.

remaining_evidence: commercial-strategy: An authored commercial GTM strategy and records establishing Jordan's decision authority and ownership. Implementing onboarding, lead scoring, and pricing controls supports GTM-related functionality, not ownership of commercial strategy.
partnership-wins: Executed channel-partner agreements and records establishing Jordan's role in securing them. The supplied project evidence documents no partnership wins.

revenue-growth: Verified baseline and subsequent revenue, measurement periods, and evidence tying Jordan's work to the change in a revenue-generating project. Demo Commerce explicitly has no revenue, so its feature implementation cannot substantiate measured revenue growth.

production-launch: Dated production release records and verified paying-customer transactions for a launched product. Demo Commerce is explicitly an unlaunched prototype with no customers and cannot be presented as meeting this requirement.

Rejection cause: Specific employer feedback or evaluation records identifying the reason for rejection. The generic message does not establish a cause; gaps against the supplied role requirements are not proof of why the employer rejected the application.

Client-facing implementation: Client discovery notes, requirements-to-configuration records, and client acceptance evidence identifying Jordan's contribution before claiming actual client delivery or translation of client needs. The implementation bullet positions transferable onboarding and commerce-setup work without asserting client experience.

Integration reliability: Test results, failure-handling evidence, or measured reliability for the payment setup integration before claiming reliable or production-ready integrations. The evidence supports integration implementation only.

Conversion impact: Verified funnel counts, baseline and comparison periods, and attribution evidence before claiming conversion improvement. Implemented onboarding and rules-based scoring do not establish conversion results.
